author: high
claim: If nonnegative integers a,b,c give a value F=a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc divisible by 3, then F is divisible by 9.
evidence: Put S=a+b+c and Q=a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca. Direct expansion gives F=SQ. For every integer x, x^3-x=x(x-1)(x+1) is divisible by 3, hence F≡S (mod 3). Thus 3|F implies 3|S. Also Q=S^2-3(ab+bc+ca), so 3|S implies 3|Q. Therefore 9|SQ=F.

links.statement: Divisibility by 3 of a represented value forces divisibility by 9.

author: high
claim: Every nonnegative integer N satisfying 3∤N or 9|N has an explicit representation N=a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc by nonnegative integers a,b,c.
evidence: The factorization F=(a+b+c)Q holds, where Q=a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca. If N=3t+1, take (a,b,c)=(t+1,t,t); then a+b+c=N and Q=1. If N=3t+2, take (a,b,c)=(t+1,t+1,t); again a+b+c=N and Q=1. If N=9k with k≥1, take (a,b,c)=(k+1,k,k-1); then a+b+c=3k and, from 2Q=(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2, Q=3, so F=9k=N. If N=0, take (0,0,0). All displayed entries are nonnegative.

glossary.t: the nonnegative quotient in N=3t+1 or N=3t+2
